newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bonds limp on crown, cenbank rate anxieties.
newsitem.headline: Czech bonds limp on crown, cenbank rate anxieties.

text.p: Czech bonds traded sideways on Monday as key corporate and government paper hovered above early June's all-time lows in thin activity but anxiety over central bank intentions to defend the ailing crown reigned.

The Ceska Sporitelna daily BICS index measuring the most liquid issues dipped 0.02 percent to 97.510, signalling an end to last week's technical correction when the ailing crown firmed as the government won a confidence vote, dealers said.
"I think it's a technical adjustment and the trend is downward and will continue to go downward," Matt Starr, the head of the capital markets desk at Creditanstalt Prague, told Reuters.

He said the market was hamstrung by fears that the central bank might be forced to reverse its recent easing in interest rates if another speculative run hits the Czech crown after a sharp drop in May.
"If they do that, it's a catastrophe for the market," Starr said.

The BICS slumped to an all-time low at 96.372 on June 6, ahead of a vote of confidence in the centre-right government, which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus narrowly won last week. That was down from year highs above 103 posted in April.

While Czech paper recovered some ground after the vote, the market has been skewered by prohibitively high interbank interest rates brought on by central bank attempts to squeeze out liquidity and stop short selling in the crown.

Speculative attacks on the crown -- spurred by a ballooning trade deficit and political instability -- culminated in the Czech National Bank's (CNB) decision to float the currency and on May 27, sending the crown roughly another 9 percent lower against major currencies.
The crown has recovered somewhat and was trading about six percent below its pre-float level against the dollar and 3.3 percent against the mark.
